title: Magnetic Levitation Tour
description: Guided walkthrough of the floater's gap dynamics: a target gap set by the drive, a virtual spring holding the floater against its weight, and heavy damping that settles it without bouncing.

steps.title: A disc floating over a ring of magnets
steps.body: A light disc hovers above a ring of magnets with nothing touching it. The one number this bench cares about is the air gap between them: where it settles, how fast it gets there, and what happens when you move the drive slider. Everything else is a consequence of that gap.

steps.title: Step 1 — the drive picks a target gap
steps.body: The drive slider chooses a target gap from 12 mm at zero to 34 mm at full drive. The plant does not work the lift out from the magnets: it holds the floater with a virtual spring, F = k (target − gap) with k = 180 N/m, scaled up as the drive rises. Read it as a spring-and-damper model of a levitation loop, not a field calculation.

steps.title: Step 2 — the floater sits below its target
steps.body: The 45 g floater weighs about 0.44 N, and a spring must stretch to carry a weight. So the gap settles where lift equals weight — below the target by m g / k_eff, about 4 mm at zero drive and about 2.5 mm at full drive.

steps.title: Step 3 — damping, so it settles without bouncing
steps.body: The 14 N·s/m damping term stands in for eddy-current drag. Against a 45 g mass and a spring this stiff it is heavily overdamped (a damping ratio around 2 to 3), so after you move the drive slider the gap creeps to its new value rather than oscillating around it. A real passive levitator is far more delicate: Earnshaw's theorem says static magnets alone cannot hold a stable float, which is why real ones lean on motion, eddy currents or feedback.

steps.title: Step 4 — reading B, F and RPM
steps.body: The lift F_z is the spring force, clamped at zero. The B readout is a separate order-of-magnitude estimate that falls roughly as 1/gap; as written it lands in the micro-tesla range, orders below a real magnet ring, so read it for its trend only and never as an input to the lift. The RPM figure is a proxy that rises with drive and with how close the gap is to its target — there is no spinning rotor.

steps.title: What this model is not
steps.body: A one-degree-of-freedom gap ODE: a mass on a virtual spring and damper, between stops at 4 mm and 60 mm. It is not a maglev-train or bearing model — no finite-element field solution, no lateral or tilt stability, no eddy-current computation, no control loop. The ring of coloured magnets is a visual cue, not the source of the force. Use it to see how a levitated mass settles, not to size a levitator.
